territorial_scope.description: Applies to platforms defined by at least 1,000,000 California users, not by where they are based, and to content concerning elections in California; the text does not state where platforms must be located.

summary.short: Requires large online platforms to remove or label materially deceptive election deepfakes and to run a reporting process for Californians, during periods before and after California elections. Allows candidates, officials and prosecutors to seek injunctive relief against platforms.
summary.long: Adds Chapter 7 (Defending Democracy from Deepfake Deception Act of 2024) to the Elections Code and amends Code of Civil Procedure § 35 to give precedence to actions under it. Covers large online platforms (public-facing websites, apps or search engines with at least 1,000,000 California users in the preceding 12 months) and audio or visual materially deceptive content, including deepfakes and chatbot output. Platforms must use state-of-the-art techniques to remove, within 72 hours of a report, deceptive content depicting candidates, elections officials or elected officials, from 120 days before a California election through election day (60 days after for elections-official content). A candidate may avoid removal of self-portrayals by including a 'manipulated' disclosure. Platforms must label other deceptive election content, within 72 hours of a report, from six months before an election. They must provide a reporting channel for California residents and respond within 36 hours. Candidates, elected and elections officials, the Attorney General, and district or city attorneys may seek injunctive relief. Newspapers, broadcasting stations and satire or parody are exempt. The text sets no fines.

notes: The registry status 'repealed' is not stated in this text, which contains no repeal clause of its own. CCP § 35(b) in SEC. 1 and 1.5 says the section is repealed on January 1, 2027 unless extended; SEC. 2 and 2.5 become operative January 1, 2027. The new Elections Code chapter has no sunset in the text. Four alternative versions of CCP § 35 exist with different precedence lists (SEC. 1.5 adds 20010 and 20012; SEC. 2 omits 20010 and 20012; SEC. 2.5 lists only 20012). SEC. 4 and 5 determine which version operates, so the amendments are conditional. The addressees (large online platforms) are a defined class, not named firms, so no firm entities are listed. Only relations, entities and notes are filled in this pass; the annotation is based on the chaptered text as provided.

“Advertisement” means any general or public communication that a large online platform knows is authorized or paid for with the purpose of supporting or opposing a candidate for elective office.
“Broadcasting station” means a radio or television broadcasting station, including any of the following:
“Candidate” means any person running for a voter-nominated office as defined in Section 359.5

“Deepfake” means audio or visual media that is digitally created or modified such that it would falsely appear to a reasonable person to be an authentic record of the actual speech or conduct of the individual depicted in the media.
“Election communication” means a general or public communication that is not an “advertisement” and that concerns any of the following:

“Election in California” means any election where a candidate, as defined in this section, is on the ballot, and any election where a statewide initiative or statewide referendum measure is on the ballot.
“Elections official” means either of the following persons acting in their official capacity:
“Large online platform” means a public-facing internet website, web application, or digital application
“Materially deceptive content” means audio or visual media that is digitally created or modified

obligations.summary: Courts must place proceedings in actions under Chapter 7 (commencing with Section 20510) of Division 20 of the Elections Code on the calendar in filing order and give them precedence (amended Code of Civil Procedure § 35(a)).
obligations.applies_from: Sec. 1 version applies until January 1, 2027 (CCP § 35(b)); Sec. 2 version operative January 1, 2027 (CCP § 35(b))
obligations.conditional_on: Applies to actions under Chapter 7 of Division 20 of the Elections Code, which are added to the list of precedence actions by this bill.

evidence.quote: shall be placed on the calendar in the order of their date of filing and shall be given precedence.

obligations.summary: Large online platforms must develop and implement procedures to identify and remove materially deceptive election content meeting listed conditions, remove qualifying posts within 72 hours of a report, and remove identical or substantially similar previously removed content during the applicable period.
obligations.conditional_on: Content reported under Section 20515(a); content posted during the period beginning 120 days before an election in California through election day (or through the 60th day after the election for content about elections officials); platform knows or acts with reckless disregard; content is about a candidate, elections official or elected official as specified.

evidence.quote: Any large online platform shall develop and implement procedures for the use of state-of-the-art techniques to identify and remove materially deceptive content

obligations.summary: Candidates for elective office must include the disclosure "This _____ has been manipulated." (image, audio or video) when portraying themselves as doing or saying something they did not do or say, during the period beginning 120 days before an election through election day. Applies to candidates who publish such content; addressee role is the closest available.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies during the period beginning 120 days before an election in California and through the day of the election; the disclosure requirement is the condition for the exception in Section 20513(d)(1).

evidence.quote: any candidate for elective office shall include the disclosure required by subdivision (d)

obligations.summary: Large online platforms must develop and implement procedures to identify materially deceptive content and label it "This _____ has been manipulated and is not authentic." within 72 hours of a report, with a clickable explanation, for content outside the Section 20513 removal rules or within advertisements and election communications.
obligations.conditional_on: Content reported under Section 20515(a); content outside the period in Section 20513(e) or within an advertisement or election communication not subject to Section 20513; labelling periods in Section 20514(e) (six months before the election through election day, or the 60th day after the election for specified content).

evidence.quote: Any large online platform shall develop and implement procedures for the use of state-of-the-art techniques to identify materially deceptive content and for labeling such content

obligations.summary: Large online platforms must provide an easily accessible way for California residents to report content that should be removed or labelled, and must respond to the reporter within 36 hours describing action taken or not taken.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies to content that should be removed under Section 20513 or labelled under Section 20514.

evidence.quote: A large online platform shall provide an easily accessible way for California residents to report to that platform content that should be removed pursuant to Section 20513 or labeled pursuant to Section 20514.

obligations.summary: Where the content is not in English, the candidate disclosure under Section 20513(d) and the platform label under Section 20514 must appear in the language used as well as in English.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies where the language of the materially deceptive content is not English.

evidence.quote: the disclosure required by subdivision (d) of Section 20513 and the label required by Section 20514 must appear in the language used as well as in English.
